Package dev.morphia

Class MorphiaBulkWriteException

java.lang.Object
java.lang.Throwable
java.lang.Exception
java.lang.RuntimeException
com.mongodb.MongoException
com.mongodb.MongoServerException
com.mongodb.MongoBulkWriteException
dev.morphia.MorphiaBulkWriteException
All Implemented Interfaces:
Serializable
public class MorphiaBulkWriteException extends MongoBulkWriteException
Thrown when a list insert or save (Datastore.insert(List, InsertManyOptions), Datastore.save(List, InsertManyOptions)) stores some entities but not others.

getFailedEntities() are the entities that were rejected, and getUnprocessedEntities() are those not written because the write stopped at a failure. Together they are exactly the entities that weren't stored, and they can be retried: ids that Morphia generated for them are cleared so a retry inserts them again. Indexes, here and in MongoBulkWriteException.getWriteErrors(), refer to positions in the list that was passed in.

Inside a transaction, a server write error aborts the transaction, so nothing is stored unless the transaction is retried and commits. List writes in a transaction stop at the first failure even when unordered; the rest are reported as unprocessed, though the server may already have attempted some of them before the transaction aborted. After a server write error, Morphia rolls back the version bumps and generated ids of every entity in the write, not just the listed ones. A version conflict doesn't abort the transaction, so the entities saved before it keep their ids and versions and can still be committed.

If a list write later fails with an error that isn't about individual entities (a network error, say), that error is thrown instead, with a MorphiaBulkWriteException attached as a suppressed exception. It lists the failures recorded so far and, as unprocessed, the entities never sent; the entities in the write that failed aren't listed, since their outcome is unknown.

When the only failures are version conflicts, no server reported an error, and MongoBulkWriteException.getServerAddress() returns the driver's default address.

Since:
3.0
